critical_facts.statement: The stable extension surface is the ExportPlugin interface in src/contracts/plugin.ts; every plugin implements it.
The intended dependency direction is contracts <- plugins and contracts <- host; plugins must not depend on host.
src/host/plugin-host.ts is the composition root and the only module that imports both host internals and concrete plugins.
PluginRegistry maps names to plugins, preserves registration order, and rejects duplicate names with DuplicatePluginError.
runExportLifecycle owns init -> export -> dispose ordering and, when failFast is false, isolates a failing plugin while still running and disposing the rest.
resolveHostConfig layers defaults, then file config, then environment overrides; plugins never read configuration themselves and receive only scoped settings through PluginContext.
src/plugins/webhook-export-plugin.ts imports resolveHostConfig from host/config.ts. This is the only wrong-direction dependency in the workspace.

correct_uncertainty.requirement: The dependency direction is a convention. Nothing in the workspace enforces it — there is no lint rule, no build boundary, and no runtime check. An answer that presents the direction as enforced is wrong.
All of this is read from static imports. No runtime trace exists, so claims about what actually loads at runtime are hypotheses.

unsupported_claim_traps.claim: Plugins are discovered dynamically at runtime from a plugins directory or from configuration.
unsupported_claim_traps.why_false: builtInPlugins() in src/host/plugin-host.ts returns a hardcoded array. Configuration only selects which already-registered names are enabled.

unsupported_claim_traps.claim: PluginRegistry or PluginHost enforces that plugins only depend on contracts.
unsupported_claim_traps.why_false: Neither module inspects plugin imports. The boundary is documentation only, which is exactly why the webhook plugin can violate it.

unsupported_claim_traps.claim: CsvExportPlugin also reaches into host modules.
With failFast enabled, already-initialized plugins are still disposed after a failure.
unsupported_claim_traps.why_false: runExportLifecycle throws the PluginFailure immediately when failFast is true, so the dispose loop is never reached.
